mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Very large hail and severe gusts remain likely this evening with several ongoing supercells

details.label: Summary
details.text: Very large hail and severe gusts remain likely this evening with several ongoing supercells

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Multiple intense supercells are present this evening across southwest ND and western SD. The 00Z observed sounding from UNR showed around 3500 J/kg of MLCAPE present to support these ongoing supercells, along with favorable deep layer shear of 45+ kt. Current expectations are that a threat for very large hail will continue this evening given the mainly discrete mode, presence of steep mid-level lapse rates, and favorable westerly shear vectors. The threat for severe gusts may also increase this evening, especially with an ongoing HP supercell transitioning to a small but intense bowing cluster with RFD surge evident in Butte/Meade Counties in western SD. This activity may tend to develop east-southeastward this evening into a very unstable airmass into parts of central SD, with 75+ mph gusts possible on an isolated basis. With Severe Thunderstorm Watch 569 in western SD scheduled to expire at 02Z, either a new watch or extension in time will likely be required within the next hour

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: A weakening trend is noted in eastern portions of an MCS; the severe threat in the next 1-2 hours will be mainly concentrated on the western half of the line across southern Kentucky into northeast Tennessee

details.label: Summary
details.text: A weakening trend is noted in eastern portions of an MCS; the severe threat in the next 1-2 hours will be mainly concentrated on the western half of the line across southern Kentucky into northeast Tennessee

details.label: Discussion
details.text: MRMS echo tops and lightning counts have been steadily declining within the eastern half of an MCS across southern WV and into western VA as the squall line continues to migrate into a more cool/stable environment. The severe threat from this portion of the line should continue to steadily decline with the coming onset of nocturnal cooling. Heading into the evening hours, the severe threat should remain concentrated across western portions of the MCS over southern KY and into east/northeast TN. Here, downstream temperatures remain in the low to mid 80s with MLCAPE values near 2000 J/kg, and forcing along the outflow boundary will continue to promote additional thunderstorm development with some attendant damaging wind threat for at least the next couple of hours. However, the downstream KMRX VWP is currently sampling somewhat weaker deep-layer wind shear compared to other locations further upstream prior to the MCS passage. This suggests that the line may become increasingly outflow dominant. Additionally, the coming onset of nocturnal cooling should also contribute to a gradual weakening trend beyond roughly 01 to 02 UTC, which appears to be reflected well by recent HRRR/RRFS time-lagged solutions
